review_candidates.title: NOC - Technical Leader
review_candidates.description: NOC Technical Leader   The Technical Lead role should help us build a team that can handle more complexity and scale without increasing in size proportionally and without becoming reliant on a few technical experts.   How would it be like to work as a NOC Technical Lead with us?  Your main mission will be to help increase the team's technical capability, autonomy, and scalability in collaboration with the NOC Manager.  You’ll be a technical point of reference for your colleagues and support them in handling complex incidents and troubleshooting activities in areas like routing, switching, VPN, VoIP, DNS, cloud, and other IT&C services – technologies that are already part of the team’s area of responsibility.  You’ll serve as the technical escalation point for situations that exceed the team’s autonomy level and contribute to identifying and implementing technical solutions.  Your role will go beyond solving individual incidents: you’ll look to identify recurring problems, understand their causes, and help implement solutions that reduce the likelihood of the same issues happening again. The Technical Lead will work closely with the NOC Manager, contributing to the development of the team's technical capabilities, managing complex situations, and continuously improving technical processes and practices. Technical leadership You will: • be a technical reference point and escalation point for complex situations; • guide troubleshooting and root cause analysis for high-impact or recurring incidents; • support the team in making technical decisions; • identify risks, recurring issues, and areas for improvement, and help implement corrective actions; • collaborate with other technical teams to solve problems requiring cross-functional expertise; • contribute to defining and improving technical standards, troubleshooting methodologies, and operational best practices; • provide technical recommendations to the NOC Manager when a problem impacts operations, resources, services, or customers; • help assess the technical impact of proposed changes and solutions.   Scaling & Continuous Improvement An important part of your role will be to help the team handle a larger volume and level of complexity, without this automatically meaning a proportional increase in resources. You will: • identify repetitive activities and automation opportunities; • simplify and improve processes and troubleshooting workflows; • contribute to developing procedures, runbooks, and technical documentation; • turn individual knowledge into reusable knowledge for the whole team; • analyze patterns in incidents and escalations to identify systemic issues; • suggest improvements to tools and processes that can reduce resolution time and manual tasks; • help define and track relevant technical metrics; • monitor the increase in the percentage of issues resolved independently by the team; • collaborate with the NOC Manager to prioritize and implement improvement initiatives that impact NOC operations. Your success won't just be measured by how many complex problems you manage to solve, but more importantly by how many problems the team becomes capable of solving without depending on you.   Mentorship & team development You'll have an active role in developing your colleagues' technical skills. You will: • mentor colleagues on day-to-day technical challenges; • use complex incidents as coaching and learning opportunities, without automatically taking over their resolution; • provide structured technical feedback and help colleagues identify their areas for growth; • organize knowledge sharing sessions, technical deep-dives, and incident reviews; • contribute to onboarding new colleagues and accelerating their technical development; • identify knowledge gaps within the team and help define training plans; • encourage colleagues to progressively take ownership of increasingly complex situations; • help build an environment were asking questions, sharing experiences, and learning from incidents are part of the normal workflow; • give the NOC Manager technical input regarding team members' competence levels and development areas. This component builds on the approach already present in the team, where curiosity, the ability to learn new technologies, creativity, and taking responsibility are expected behaviors.
